correctness.rationale: The graph-distance condition is reduced exactly to cyclic 111 avoidance without the hub or to a rim edge with the hub. Run-by-run addition testing forces all zero-blocks to have length one or two, with a length-two block flanked by length-two one-blocks. A 2-state cyclic transfer yields the formal log determinant coefficient; its trace normalization was justified by run anchoring. Tight cardinality classifications and root asymptotics follow from the run inequalities and a reciprocal sextic. Direct BFS-geodesic enumeration of every vertex subset for n=5 through 13 matches every polynomial coefficient and each extremal count. The proof covers all integers \(n\ge5\); finite tests are supplemental.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the full labeled inclusion-maximal general-position polynomial for every wheel with at least five rim vertices, its exact structural classification, and its extremal coefficient/asymptotic consequences. Accessible full texts establish the wheel maximum cardinality, ordinary all-set graph-join polynomial, or lower/terminal general-position parameters, not the maximal-set distribution. value.rationale: Inclusion-maximal general-position sets quantify the whole spectrum of greedy terminal placements, a distinct structural question from the previously studied largest or smallest cardinalities and the ordinary all-set polynomial. The theorem gives a complete structural classification, a closed two-variable enumeration, sharp modulo-dependent counts of both extremal rim families and exponential growth with a precisely characterized base. The wheel is a canonical nontrivial graph family; these are motivated global invariants rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a normalization check.
